newsitem.title: ESTONIA: CREDIT RATING EXPECTED BEFORE END OF YEAR.
newsitem.headline: CREDIT RATING EXPECTED BEFORE END OF YEAR.

text.p: An Estonian finance ministry official on Tuesday said the country requested a credit rating from Moody's and it may be obtained before the end of the year.

"We are expecting to obtain it before the end of the year," said Agu Lellep, permanent undersecretary of the ministry of finance, in a speech due to be made at a Baltic capital investment conference in Stockholm on Wednesday.

The central bank said last month that it has decided to order a credit rating for the country after a long period of delay, fearing that investor interest in Estonia would increase after the rating, heightening fears of an over-heating economy.
Lellep also said in his speech that the integration of Estonia's financial system into world markets continued.
"Estonian banks have fast increasing access to external medium-term and long-term funding, mostly from international financial institutions," he said.
As a result, the share of medium-term loans in commercial banks' portfolios was increasing, accompanied by a gradual decline in domestic lending rates, Lellep said.
Lellep also mentioned the successful start of the local bourse over a short period of time.
He added that some 39 public securities issues worth 1.3 billion kroons were registered last year.
Bond market capitalisation accounts for 17 percent of the whole securities market capitalisation, he added.
Lellep will be accompanied by representatives of the Estonian central bank, the ministry of economy and the Tallinn bourse at the Stockholm conference.
